thread:
alex: Hey team — enterprise customer (Org: BrightDocs) hit a 413 when calling /v1/rerank. They say they didn't send huge files, just a long query + ~80 docs. Error: "413 Payload Too Large" with body 'request size exceeded'. No per-doc info.

maria: Thanks @alex. Do we have the original request payload (sanitized)?

alex: Pasting minimal repro (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>

{
  "query": "<~6000 char user query about legal regs>",
  "documents": ["<doc1 text length ~12000 chars>", "<doc2>" ... ~80 items]
}
```

Response: 413 + message above. Customer expects clearer guidance (they tried chunking but unsure how to calc limits).

maria: Ok. Preliminary triage: could be combined token limit (query + sum(docs)) or per-document char cap or total payload size. We need exact limit and an error that tells which constraint tripped. Escalating to eng if we can't reproduce.

jordan: I can repro locally. If you include large raw docs as strings the request body can exceed our NGINX/nginx-ingress body size OR we hit internal reranker token limit. Two different failure modes:
- nginx 413: request entity too large (body bytes)
- service 413/422: combined token char limit exceeded (we should return a 400 with details, we currently don't).

I ran curl with their payload and adding `--trace-ascii` shows HTTP 413 comes from the ingress layer before our app. So it's body bytes not token accounting in this case.

maria: Good catch. So customer's stack hit ingress limit. We should advise them to switch to sending document references (ids/urls) or chunk content and call rerank in batches. Also update UX to suggest chunking.

alex: They want a recommended chunking recipe and example code. Also want to know how to compute combined tokens for our reranker so they can pre-check before sending.

sam: Docs suggestion: add a section under Rerank troubleshooting -> "Request too large / 413" with:
- brief explanation of both byte-size and token-size causes
- sample curl showing streaming/chunked approach and batching docs into groups of N where N is computed by heuristics (chars->tokens)
- example error text we should surface: "Request rejected: total tokens (query + docs) = X, limit = Y. Reduce docs or chunk. If body bytes > 6MB, consider sending doc references."

jordan: For heuristics: assume 4 chars per token for english avg. So tokens ~= ceil(chars/4). Our reranker currently has a hard limit of 20480 tokens combined (query+docs). For bytes/ingress default nginx on some configs it's 6MB. We should not leak both numbers as absolute but provide them as guidance per deployment tier. Hosted customers: limit = 20480 tokens; Dedicated/private may vary.

maria: Action items:
- jordan: can you add a diagnostic that, when our service rejects for token limit, returns JSON {"error":"tokens_exceeded", "query_tokens":X, "docs_tokens":Y, "limit":Z} ? (we need it to be backwards compatible and not change status code if it's ingress 413).
- sam: update docs with chunking examples and curl samples + recommended batching script.
- support: send interim reply to customer explaining both possible causes and giving a quick workaround.

jordan: Yep. I'll add the token diagnostic and a guard that returns 400 with that JSON for service-level token checks. Can't change nginx timeouts/body limits — for those we'll add text in error recommending doc references.

maria: Draft reply to customer (sent):
"Hi — thanks for the report. We see a 413 from the edge when raw docs are included. This usually means the HTTP body exceeds the edge limit OR the combined token limit is exceeded. Quick fixes: 1) send doc references (S3/GCS URLs) instead of raw text; 2) split the documents into batches (e.g., 10-20 docs per rerank request) and merge results client-side; 3) shorten query/ask. We're implementing clearer diagnostic error messages so you'll get token counts in future. I'll follow up once eng pushes the change." :thumbsup:

alex: Customer replied: they'd prefer server-side chunking/fallback if possible (i.e., accept big payload, internally split, and return partial ranked results). Is that something we can do?

jordan: That would be a bigger infra change — accepting huge payloads would blow memory and increases DoS surface. Not safe. We can offer a helper library that performs client-side chunking+merging and can be used server-side in Dedicated if customer wants.

maria: Ok. I'll ask Solutions to propose the helper library as a quick deliverable. Sam, add a KB article with example Python helper that: computes tokens via heuristic, batches docs so combined tokens <= 12k (safe margin), calls /v1/rerank for each batch, then merges ranking scores by re-sorting with normalized scores.

sam: on it. I'll include sample code:
```
# naive batcher
def chars_to_tokens(chars):
  return (chars + 3) // 4

# build batches until sum(tokens) + query_tokens > limit
```

support-bot: Ticket #INC-8342 created and linked to thread. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-runtime, docs.

maria: Thanks all. Jordan — ping here when you have the token diagnostic PR so I can notify customer. Sam — please link KB in reply.

jordan: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/712 — adds 400 token diagnostic for service-level limits and tests. ETA review: EOD.
